RF.K.2.c|K.why: EE descriptor describes matching onsets (EE.RF.K.2.d), not identifying syllables.
suggested: I can blend and break apart onsets and rimes in new words and make new rhyming words by changing the onset.
I can blend and segment the onset and rime of single-syllable spoken words (c-at, cat).
I can blend an onset and rime when an adult says them slowly (m-op) with support.
I can say the first sound of a spoken word with help.
I can, with support, identify the syllables in spoken words by clapping or tapping.

RF.K.4|K.why: EE descriptor describes independent book exploration, not purposeful shared reading of a familiar text.
suggested: I can read emergent-reader books on my own and tell what happened and why I read them.
I can read emergent-reader texts with purpose and understanding.
I can read along with an adult and point to words I know in a simple book.
I can look at pictures and tell what a simple book is about with help.
I can take part in shared reading of a familiar text for a purpose, such as finding a favourite page.

W.K.2.a|K.why: EE descriptor describes sharing information about a topic, not stating an opinion.
suggested: I can draw, tell and write my opinion about a book or topic and give a reason.
I can draw, tell and write to name a topic or book and state my opinion about it.
I can draw a picture and tell an adult what I like or do not like about a book.
I can point to a picture to show which book or thing I like with help.
I can, with support, draw, dictate or write to state my opinion.

L.K.1.a|K.why: EE descriptor describes telling letters from symbols, not noticing linguistic diversity.
suggested: I can share words from my home language and learn words from my classmates' languages.
I can recognize and appreciate that people in my school speak different languages.
I can name one language other than English that someone in my class speaks with support.
I can notice that some people say words differently with help.
I can, with support, notice that people around me use different languages.

L.K.2.a|K.why: EE descriptor describes early writing, not understanding words used in everyday routines.
suggested: I can explain two meanings of a word like duck or tie and use each in a sentence.
I can recognize that some words have more than one meaning (duck, tie).
I can match a multiple-meaning word to two pictures with support.
I can point to a picture that matches a word I hear with help.
I can, with support, show I understand words used in everyday routines, such as line up or lunch.

L.K.5.a|K.why: EE descriptor describes sorting objects into categories, not telling letters from other symbols.
suggested: I can use nouns, verbs and prepositions correctly in longer spoken sentences.
I can use frequently used nouns, verbs and prepositions when I speak.
I can name objects and actions in a picture with support.
I can point to the object or action an adult names with help.
I can, with support, tell letters apart from other symbols or shapes.

L.K.5.b|K.why: EE descriptor describes opposites, not using frequently occurring nouns.
suggested: I can say plural nouns correctly, including some irregular ones like mice and feet.
I can say plural nouns correctly by adding -s or -es (dog, dogs; wish, wishes).
I can say the plural of a familiar noun when an adult models it.
I can show one or many objects when asked with help.
I can, with support, use frequently occurring nouns when I communicate.

L.K.5.c|K.why: EE descriptor describes using words to communicate, not frequently occurring plural nouns.
suggested: I can use question words to ask my own questions about a story or topic.
I can understand and use question words such as who, what, where and when.
I can answer a who or what question about a picture with support.
I can point to the answer to a who question with help.
I can, with support, use frequently occurring plural nouns.

L.K.5.d|K.why: EE descriptor describes common verbs, not answering simple questions, prepositions or linking words.
suggested: I can say longer, expanded sentences that add details about who, what and where.
I can say complete sentences and expand them by adding a describing word or detail.
I can repeat a complete sentence after an adult model.
I can say two words together to share an idea with help.
I can, with support, choose answers to simple who and what questions, understand on, off, in and out, and link two words together.

RF.1.2.b|1.why: EE descriptor describes counting syllables, not matching segmented phonemes to pictures.
suggested: I can blend sounds in longer words with consonant blends, like s-t-o-p, and say the word quickly.
I can blend sounds to say single-syllable words, including words with consonant blends.
I can blend three sounds (c-a-t) to say a word with support.
I can say a word after an adult blends the sounds for me.
I can, with support, match sounds said one at a time (c-a-t) to the picture of that word.

RF.1.3.a|1.why: CC Emerging and EE descriptors describe initial phonemes, not digraphs or upper-case letters.
suggested: I can read and spell new words that have digraphs like sh, ch, th and wh.
I can say the sounds of common consonant digraphs (sh, ch, th, wh).
I can say the sound of sh or ch when I see it in a familiar word with support.
I can match a digraph card to a picture with help.
I can recognize and name upper-case letters of the alphabet.

RF.1.4.a|1.why: CC Emerging descriptor describes silent book exploration, which is an EE-level skill, not reading grade-level text.
suggested: I can read grade-level text with purpose and understanding and retell it in my own words.
I can read grade-level text with purpose and understanding.
I can read simple books with help and use pictures to understand.
I can read a few familiar words in a simple book with help.
I can take part in shared reading of different kinds of texts.

L.1.1|1.why: CC Emerging and EE descriptors describe writing own name, not linguistic diversity.
suggested: I can share and compare how words are said in different languages in my class.
I can recognize and appreciate that people in my school and community speak different languages.
I can name a language someone in my class speaks with support.
I can notice that people speak in different ways with help.
I can notice that people around me use different languages.

L.1.2.a|1.why: EE descriptor describes the first letter of own name, not understanding everyday-routine words.
suggested: I can use word endings like -s, -ed and -ing to work out new words in my reading.
I can use word endings like -s and -ed as clues to what an unknown word means (looks, looked).
I can use word endings to work out new words with some help.
I can tell when a word has an ending added with help.
I can show I understand words used in everyday routines, such as wash hands or snack.

L.1.5.a|1.why: EE descriptor describes sorting objects, not writing letters from own name.
suggested: I can use common, proper and possessive nouns correctly in my writing and explain the difference.
I can use common, proper and possessive nouns correctly when I speak and write.
I can capitalize names and use common nouns in sentences with support.
I can name people and things in a picture with help.
I can write letters from my own name.

L.2.1.a|2.why: EE descriptor describes producing letters, not noticing linguistic diversity.
suggested: I can explain how people use different languages and ways of speaking at home, at school and in the community.
I can recognize and appreciate linguistic diversity at home, in the community and in what I read and hear.
I can name different languages people use in my school with support.
I can notice that people speak in different ways with help.
I can notice that people around me use different languages.

L.2.1.b|2.why: EE descriptor describes using nouns, not noticing formal and informal language.
suggested: I can switch between formal and informal English on purpose and explain why.
I can recognize formal and informal uses of English.
I can sort phrases into school talk and friend talk with support.
I can tell whether someone is talking to a friend or a teacher with help.
I can notice formal and informal uses of language.

L.2.3.a|2.why: EE descriptor describes informal language, not rhyme and repetition.
suggested: I can explain how alliteration, rhyme and repeated lines create rhythm and meaning in a poem or story.
I can describe how words and phrases supply rhythm and meaning in a text (alliteration, rhyme, repeated lines).
I can find rhyming or repeated words in a poem with support.
I can clap to the rhythm of a familiar rhyme with help.
I can, with support, identify rhyme and repetition in letters, words or phrases.

RF.3.3.d|3.why: School levels are inverted: Advanced describes the easiest skill and Emerging the hardest.
suggested: I can read and spell less common irregularly spelled words and explain which part is irregular.
I can read grade-appropriate irregularly spelled words accurately.
I can read common irregular words such as said and friend with some support.
I can read a few high-frequency words such as the and was with help.
I can recognize 40 or more written words.

SL.3.1.c|3.why: CC descriptors describe explaining own ideas (SL.3.1.d), and the EE descriptor describes linking ideas, not indicating confusion.
suggested: I can ask questions that check understanding and connect my comments to several classmates' ideas.
I can ask questions to check understanding, stay on topic and link my comments to what others say.
I can ask one question about the topic using a question starter.
I can stay on topic and say one thing about it with help.
I can show when I am confused or do not understand information.

L.3.1.b|3.why: CC descriptors describe key words and phrases (L.3.1.c), not written versus spoken English.
suggested: I can explain several differences between written and spoken English and choose the right one for my purpose.
I can recognize differences between the conventions of written and spoken English.
I can tell one difference between how I talk and how I write with support.
I can tell whether a sentence is spoken or written with help.
Not applicable

L.3.1.c|3.why: CC descriptors describe working out unknown words (L.3.2), not key words and word choice for effect.
suggested: I can explain how key words help a reader and choose vivid words for effect in my own writing.
I can identify key words and phrases that help readers understand a topic and choose words for effect.
I can find key words in a text using bold print or headings with support.
I can point to a topic word in a text with help.
I can identify key words in a text.

L.3.2.b|3.why: CC descriptors describe degrees of certainty (L.3.3.b), not prefixes and suffixes.
suggested: I can use prefixes and suffixes to work out and explain the meanings of many new words.
I can determine the meaning of a new word when a prefix or suffix is added (happy, unhappy).
I can find a prefix or suffix in a word and use a chart to guess its meaning.
I can find a small word I know inside a longer word with help.
I can, with support, tell the time meaning of verbs when -ing or -ed is added.

L.3.2.c|3.why: CC descriptors describe real-life word connections (L.3.3.c), not using resources to find word meanings.
suggested: I can choose the best resource, print or digital, to find and check word meanings.
I can use resources such as dictionaries and glossaries to determine word meanings.
I can look up a word in a picture or student dictionary with support.
I can ask an adult what a word means.
Not applicable

L.3.3.a|3.why: CC descriptors describe spatial and temporal phrases (L.3.4.a), and the EE descriptor describes making requests, not literal meaning.
suggested: I can explain the difference between literal and non-literal phrases and use some in my writing.
I can determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text and tell literal from non-literal language.
I can tell whether a phrase means exactly what it says using examples.
I can match a phrase to a picture of its meaning with help.
I can determine the literal meaning of words and phrases in context.

L.3.3.b|3.why: CC descriptors describe grammar conventions, and the EE descriptor describes commenting, not degrees of certainty or real-life word connections.
suggested: I can choose words that show exactly how sure someone is and explain the difference.
I can distinguish shades of meaning among words that describe degrees of certainty (knew, believed, suspected).
I can put certainty words in order from least to most sure using a scale.
I can tell the difference between know and think with help.
I can identify real-life connections between words and how they are used.

L.3.3.c|3.why: CC descriptors describe verb tense, not connecting words to real-life use.
suggested: I can connect new words to my experiences and other words I know to remember and use them.
I can make connections between words and how they are used in real life.
I can connect a new word to something I have seen or done with support.
I can match a word to a real-life picture with help.
I can identify words that describe how I feel.

L.3.4.a|3.why: CC descriptors describe subject-verb agreement, and the EE descriptor is general vocabulary, not spatial and temporal words.
suggested: I can use varied phrases that show time and place to make my writing clear and interesting.
I can identify and use phrases that signal spatial and temporal relationships (after dinner that night).
I can use time and place words such as before, after and under from a word bank.
I can follow directions with under or behind with help.
I can understand words that show place and time, such as behind, under, after and later.

L.3.5.b|3.why: CC descriptors describe easily confused words (L.3.5.e), and the EE descriptor describes real-life word connections, not verb tense.
suggested: I can use past, present and future tenses correctly and keep my tense consistent.
I can use simple verb tenses (I walked, I walk, I will walk) correctly.
I can choose the correct tense of a verb in a sentence with support.
I can tell whether something happened yesterday or today with help.
I can use present and past tense verbs.

L.3.5.c|3.why: CC descriptors describe capitalization and punctuation, and the EE descriptor describes feeling words, not subject-verb agreement.
suggested: I can find and fix subject-verb agreement errors in my own and others' writing.
I can make subjects and verbs agree in my sentences (he runs, they run).
I can choose the verb that matches the subject in a sentence with support.
I can say a simple sentence with a subject and verb using a model.
I can combine words such as noun and verb, or subject, verb and object, when I communicate.

L.3.5.e|3.why: EE descriptor describes feeling words, not easily confused words.
suggested: I can explain the difference between easily confused words and always use the right one.
I can use easily confused words such as to, too and two correctly.
I can choose the right word (to, too, two) in a sentence using examples.
I can notice that some words sound the same with help.
I can notice easily confused words.

L.3.6.a|3.why: EE descriptor describes spatial and temporal words, not capitalizing names.
suggested: I can capitalize and format titles correctly and explain the rules I used.
I can capitalize titles correctly in my writing and explain why.
I can capitalize the first word of a title using a model.
I can find capital letters in a title with help.
I can capitalize the first letter of familiar names.

R.4.2|4.why: CC descriptors repeat the R.4.1 descriptors (details and inference), not summarizing a theme or central idea.
suggested: I can write a concise summary and explain how several key details work together to develop the theme or central idea.
I can summarize a text and determine its theme or central idea and explain how key details support it.
I can name the main idea and list two key details using a graphic organizer.
I can tell what a short text is mostly about with pictures and help.
I can identify the theme or main idea of a text.

SL.4.2|4.why: EE descriptor describes identifying the main idea, not asking and answering questions about details.
suggested: I can paraphrase longer parts of a text or presentation accurately and explain the key points.
I can paraphrase parts of a text read aloud or information presented in different media.
I can retell one part of what I heard in my own words using a sentence frame.
I can repeat one detail I heard with help.
I can ask and answer questions about details from a text read aloud or information presented orally or in other media.

L.4.1.d|4.why: EE descriptor describes comparative and superlative adjectives, not choosing punctuation.
suggested: I can choose punctuation such as exclamation marks, commas or ellipses on purpose and explain the effect.
I can choose punctuation for effect in my writing.
I can choose a period, question mark or exclamation mark for a sentence with support.
I can find the end mark in a sentence with help.
I can choose the right punctuation for a sentence.

L.4.2.a|4.why: EE descriptor describes capitalizing the first word, not using context to choose a word.
suggested: I can use several kinds of context clues to work out and check the meaning of new words and phrases.
I can use context as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.
I can use the words around a new word to guess its meaning with support.
I can use a picture to work out a new word with help.
I can use context to choose a word that completes a sentence read aloud by an adult.

L.4.3.a|4.why: EE descriptor describes expressing emotion, not literal word meaning.
suggested: I can explain what similes and metaphors mean and how they help the reader picture an idea.
I can determine the meaning of words and phrases in a text, including similes and metaphors.
I can explain a simple simile using a picture or example.
I can tell whether a phrase is silly or real with help.
I can determine the literal meaning of words and phrases in context.

L.4.3.c|4.why: EE descriptor describes communicating with peers, not understanding opposites.
suggested: I can choose precise synonyms and antonyms to make my writing more exact and interesting.
I can understand words by relating them to their synonyms and antonyms.
I can match a word to a synonym or antonym using a chart.
I can match a word to its opposite picture with help.
I can show I understand opposites, such as hot and cold.

L.4.4.a|4.why: EE descriptor describes using context to complete a sentence (L.4.2.a), not identifying domain-specific vocabulary.
suggested: I can use precise action words and topic words accurately in my speaking and writing.
I can learn and use words that show precise actions and feelings and words basic to a topic.
I can use topic words from a word wall in my writing with support.
I can point to a picture of a topic word with help.
I can identify key subject-specific words.

L.4.5.a|4.why: CC descriptors describe grammar in general, and the EE descriptor is general grammar, not relative pronouns or possessive pronouns.
suggested: I can use relative pronouns and adverbs to combine ideas into complex sentences and explain their purpose.
I can use relative pronouns (who, which, that) and relative adverbs (where, when, why) correctly.
I can join two sentences with who or which using a model.
I can answer a who question about a picture with help.
I can use possessive pronouns such as my, your, his and her.

W.9-10.2.a|9-10.why: CC Emerging descriptor describes informative writing (W.9-10.2.b), not argument.
suggested: I can write compelling arguments and literary analysis with clear reasoning, literary theory and sufficient evidence, addressing counterclaims.
I can write arguments and literary analysis that support claims with valid reasoning and relevant, sufficient evidence.
I can write a claim with reasons and some evidence using an argument organizer.
I can state my opinion and one reason using a sentence frame with support.
I can, with support, write or dictate an argument or literary analysis with a clear claim and valid reasons.

W.9-10.3.c|9-10.why: CC Emerging descriptor describes drawing and dictating (an EE-level skill), not word choice.
suggested: I can use precise, culturally-sustaining and subject-specific language and telling details to manage complex topics vividly.
I can use culturally-sustaining language, domain-specific vocabulary, telling details and sensory language to convey a vivid picture.
I can add subject words and sensory details from a word bank to my writing.
I can use a few topic words and simple describing words with support.
N/A

L.5.6.b|5.why: CC descriptors describe reading fluency (RF.5.4), copied with the wrong standard text; L.5.6.b is italics, underlining and quotation marks with titles.
suggested: I can choose italics, underlining or quotation marks correctly for any kind of title and explain the rule.
I can use italics, underlining or quotation marks correctly to show titles of works.
I can put quotation marks around a story title using a model.
I can find a title in a sentence with help.
Not applicable

L.5.6.c|5.why: CC descriptors describe oral reading fluency (RF.5.4.b), copied with the wrong standard text; L.5.6.c is spelling with reference materials.
suggested: I can spell grade-level and challenging words correctly and use several reference tools to check and edit my work.
I can spell grade-level words correctly, using reference materials to solve words and edit my writing.
I can spell common words correctly and use a dictionary or spell-checker with support.
I can spell a few familiar words and copy others from a word wall with help.
I can spell untaught words by sounding them out and using common spelling patterns.
